subject: Hosted API: speed bands proposal & temporary SLO adjustment request
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@optimahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, Apr 05 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API: speed bands proposal & temporary SLO adjustment request

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for taking the call last week. As discussed, we ran a short analysis of your early production traffic and drafted a pragmatic path to get you through onboarding without triggering noisy SLA escalations while we finish the traffic shaping and caching rules on your side. Summary of the ask below:

Proposal (short):
- Temporary measurement adjustment for Hosted API responses for a 14-day onboarding window.
- Apply "speed bands" so we separately measure interactive (single-shot chat) and batch (bulk inference) traffic.
- Targeted commitments during the window: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 350ms for interactive traffic; batch traffic excluded from p50 targets and measured separately.
- Measurement detail: 1-minute rolling buckets and 1-minute sliding percentiles (rather than a 5-minute aggregation) to avoid penalizing short bursts tied to import jobs.

Why this helps:
- Your current import spikes (30–90s bursts) would otherwise inflate p95 when measured over coarse windows. The 1-minute rolling approach minimizes false-positive breaches while we tune client-side retry/jitter and routing.

Safety controls and limits:
- The change is explicitly temporary (14 days) and will revert automatically unless we agree on an extension.
- SLA credits remain tied to sustained degradation (sustained >= 10 minutes of p95 breach for interactive class). Short, isolated bursts within a 1–2 minute span do not trigger credits under the proposed policy.
- We will enable a fallback routing policy: if p95 crosses 500ms for >3 consecutive 1-minute buckets, requests automatically route to an alternate instance pool.

Attachments: SLO-proposal-v1.xlsx (proposal + measurement recipe), sample-traffic-logs-20270401.txt (subset of your traffic we analyzed).

Would you be open to this temporary approach while we ship the client-side optimizations and caching rules? If yes, I can: (1) send an updated proposal to sign (DocuSign), (2) schedule a 30-min tech sync with Marcus to review measurement/observability, and (3) have Ben loop Procurement for the contract language.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks for the clear write-up. A few quick clarifying questions before we take this to procurement: 

1) Can you confirm the behavior around SLA credits? Our legal wants to ensure a temporary window doesn't remove detection for real outages. Your note about sustained >=10 minutes is helpful — please put that precisely in the SLO language.
2) How will observability look from our side? We need a dashboard or a read-only view into the 1-minute buckets and the raw latencies so our SREs can validate during the window.
3) What rollback options do we have if the temporary policy increases errors or causes regressions?

Also — procurement will want the DocuSign and a short summary of who signs what. Can Ben share a one-page amendment text that our legal can attach to the MSA?

If everything checks out I'll ask procurement to review and we can schedule the tech sync.

Best,
Olivia Park

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Cc: Kim Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, Apr 06 2027 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API: speed bands proposal & temporary SLO adjustment request

Hi Olivia — thanks for the questions, answers inline and next steps below. Quoting your items for clarity.

> 1) Can you confirm the behavior around SLA credits?

Yes. Precise language we'll include in the amendment: 
- "Sustained Service Degradation" means any interactive-class p95 latency breach where p95 >= 500ms for at least 10 continuous minutes. Only Sustained Service Degradations are eligible for SLA credits. Short bursts that raise p95 in isolated 1-minute buckets are explicitly excluded from credit calculations during the temporary onboarding window.

> 2) How will observability look from our side?

We'll provision a read-only dashboard in the Redwood Console scoped to your account and the "onboarding window" measurement view. Features:
- 1-minute histogram and rolling p50/p95 lines for interactive/batch classes.
- Downloadable raw 1-minute bucket CSVs for the period.
- Alerting channel to your Ops slack channel we can wire.
Marcus will join the tech sync and show the dashboard live.

> 3) What rollback options do we have if the temporary policy increases errors or causes regressions?

Rollback plan (automated + manual):
- Automated: if interactive p95 >= 500ms for 3 consecutive 1-minute buckets we automatically route new requests to an alternate instance pool and notify both teams.
- Manual: either side can terminate the adjustment and revert to standard 5-minute measurement within 15 minutes of formal notice. We'll add a 30-minute post-rollback monitoring window.

Procurement note: Ben, can you produce a one-page amendment that states the temporary measurement adjustment, the exact SLO language above, the 14-day window, and signature blocks for Optima + Redwood? Please also include the DocuSign stub link.

Next steps:
- Ben to draft amendment & DocuSign (today)
- Marcus to prepare a 30-min tech sync (tomorrow) with a sample dashboard and CSV export
- Olivia to route amendment to procurement/legal for review

I've attached SLO-proposal-v2.xlsx with the precise wording and the measurement recipe Marcus will present.

Thanks —
Stephanie
